newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee merging oil/gas unit into Devon.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee merging oil/gas unit into Devon.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp and Devon Energy Corp said Thursday they agreed that Kerr-McGee will merge its North American onshore oil and gas exploration and production business into Devon.
In the combination, Kerr-McGee will receive 9,954,000 newly issued shares of Devon common. Simultaneously, Devon will gain proved oil and gas reserves of about 53 million barrels of oil equivalent.
Devon also will gain undeveloped leasehold (drilling rights) of 370,000 net acres.
The Kerr-McGee properties involved are concentrated in the Permian, Mid-Continent and Rocky Mountain regions of the United States and western Canada.

Proven reserves attributable to these properties are expected to be about 24 million barrels of oil and 170 billion cubic feet of gas at the time of closing. Kerr-McGee's Gulf of Mexico properties are not included.

The effective date of the transaction is expected to be December 31, 1996. At that time, Kerr-McGee will own about 31 percent of the outstanding shares of Devon common. Devon's board will be expanded to nine, composed of the six current members and three members nominated by Kerr-McGee.
Kerr-McGee chairman Frank McPherson said cash flow from properties involved in the merger represents less than 10 percent of the company's current cash flow.
"We expect virtually no effect on Kerr-McGee's earnings per share in 1997," McPherson said in a statement.

The 53 million barrels of oil equivalent (MMBoe) would substantially boost Devon's proved reserves. At the beginning of the year, Devon's reserves were estimated at 364 billion cubic feet of gas and 55 million barrels of oil and natural gas liquids, totaling about 115 MMBoe.
Like those of Kerr-McGee, most of Devon's properties are in four areas -- the Permian Basin, the Rocky Mountains, the San Juan Basin and the Mid-Continent.
The boards of both companies have approved the transaction, including a related "standstill" agreement that limits future Devon share purchases by Kerr-McGee.
